title: Settings
description: The one singleton configuration manifest, metadata.id always "default". An optional settings.yaml at an import directory's root; defaults apply when none is imported.

goalLevels.description: Display names for the three levels, in order: goal, objective, then outcome. A vault may use its own plan's words (for example Pillar for goal).

operator.description: The author recorded on a version when no one is signed in, such as a change from the command line or a local vault: the deployment or the role that runs it, never a person (TAXONOMY.md D27).

examples.description: Examples this vault shows behind the "?" on a field, in its own words, keyed by field: problem.situation, problem.cause, change.what, change.gain, aim.change, aim.gain, objective, success.statement, gap.current, gap.desired. The product ships generic examples and names no organisation; a vault that is about one supplies examples its own people recognise. A field with no entry here shows the product's own. See TAXONOMY.md D20.

chromium.description: Path to the chromium or chromium-like executable for PDF rendering. Omit it and the renderer takes the CHROMIUM environment variable, or the first chromium on PATH.

vision.description: The future the organisation is working towards.

mission.description: What the organisation does to get there.

source.description: Where the vision and mission are published.

purpose.description: Why everything below exists, stated once at the top: the vision and mission every goal serves (Kaufman's ideal vision, the Balanced Scorecard's mission and vision). See TAXONOMY.md D24.
